answer: A public nebula of recent activity vectors records each identity's transaction delta over a rolling window. New registrations pay a base fee of 50 credits, but any agent whose delta correlates above 0.7 with an existing cluster sees its fee multiplied by the cluster size. An attacker launching fifty near-identical sybils faces either costly behavioral diversification or total fees exceeding 2500 credits, while a single honest agent pays only the base once. Enforcement requires the published fee-calculation hash to match the nebula state before the identity enters the karst of admitted agents.
